latestPolicyUpdate.title: Delaware raises income threshold for Emergency Assistance eligibility
latestPolicyUpdate.summary: Effective July 1, Delaware DHSS raised the income threshold for Emergency Assistance — which covers rent, utilities, and emergency shelter — from 100% to 125% of the Federal Poverty Level.

contentSource.name: Delaware Health and Social Services

latestPolicyUpdate.body:
The Delaware Department of Health and Social Services (DHSS) announced that the income eligibility threshold for the Emergency Assistance (EA) program will increase from 100% to 125% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL), effective July 1, 2026.

This change expands eligibility for thousands of Delaware households currently just above the cutoff. For a family of four, 125% FPL equals approximately $39,000 per year in 2026.

Emergency Assistance provides one-time funds for rent, utilities, and emergency shelter for households facing an unforeseen crisis. Eligible households must also receive, or be eligible for, Cash Assistance (TANF, GA, or SSI) or certain Medicaid programs.

The change affects applications processed on or after July 1. Households that were denied EA benefits in the past 90 days due to income may reapply after July 1 under the new threshold.

In Wilmington, Emergency Assistance is administered through the Porter State Service Center (509 W. 8th Street) and the Northeast State Service Center (1624 Jessup Street).
latestPolicyUpdate.author: manual
latestPolicyUpdate.why_it_matters: This is a meaningful expansion. Many working families in Wilmington earn just above the old 100% FPL cutoff and have historically been ineligible for Emergency Assistance even during a genuine crisis. The new threshold brings more households into eligibility starting July 1.

latestPolicyUpdate.title: Rodney Square Farmers Market returns June 7 — SNAP/EBT accepted
latestPolicyUpdate.summary: The Rodney Square Farmers Market opens its 2026 season on June 7. The market accepts SNAP and EBT benefits and features 20+ local vendors through October.

contentSource.name: Wilmington Farmers Market

latestPolicyUpdate.body:
The Rodney Square Farmers Market returns for its 2026 season beginning Saturday, June 7. The market will run every Saturday from 9am to 1pm through October 31, 2026, in the heart of downtown Wilmington.

This season features more than 20 confirmed local vendors offering fresh produce, dairy, proteins, baked goods, and prepared foods. The market accepts SNAP/EBT benefits, and several vendors participate in the Double Up Food Bucks program, which matches SNAP spending dollar-for-dollar on fresh fruits and vegetables up to $20 per visit.

Rodney Square is located at 1000 N. King Street, Wilmington, DE 19801. Parking is available in nearby garages. The market is accessible via DART bus routes 2, 6, and 11.

latestPolicyUpdate.why_it_matters: Rodney Square sits in a zip code with limited full-service grocery access. The market's SNAP acceptance and Double Up Food Bucks matching effectively doubles the purchasing power of food assistance benefits for fresh produce.

latestPolicyUpdate.title: Delaware Medicaid expansion covers dental for adults starting October 1
latestPolicyUpdate.summary: Delaware will begin covering comprehensive dental care for adult Medicaid enrollees on October 1, 2026 — a first for the state. This affects an estimated 70,000 Delaware adults currently on Medicaid.

contentSource.name: Delaware Health and Social Services

latestPolicyUpdate.body:
Delaware Governor announced that the state's Medicaid program will begin covering comprehensive dental care for adult enrollees starting October 1, 2026. Previously, adult Medicaid coverage in Delaware was limited to emergency dental extractions only.

The expansion includes preventive care (cleanings, X-rays), restorative services (fillings, crowns), and oral surgery. Orthodontia and cosmetic procedures are not included.

An estimated 70,000 Delaware adults currently enrolled in Medicaid will benefit from the change. No action is required by existing enrollees — coverage activates automatically on October 1.

For Wilmington residents, Ministry of Caring currently operates a dental clinic that serves low-income patients regardless of insurance status. Starting October 1, Ministry of Caring will be able to bill Medicaid directly for covered services, reducing or eliminating out-of-pocket costs for eligible patients.

Residents who are not currently enrolled in Medicaid but believe they may be eligible can apply through Delaware's ASSIST portal at assist.dhss.delaware.gov.
latestPolicyUpdate.author: manual
latestPolicyUpdate.why_it_matters: Dental care has been one of the most significant unmet health needs for low-income Delawareans. Untreated dental problems lead to missed work, school absences, and serious health complications. This expansion removes a major barrier — particularly for residents who've relied on Ministry of Caring's clinic for years.

items.summary: The Refuge, a long-term, integrated sober-living facility located in Bear, Delaware. The Refuge provides separate housing units for men and women as well as women with children. These housing environments are supervised around the clock and provide residents support to achieve their sobriety and develop necessary skills to live safely and independently in the community. Structured clinical programs provide varying intensities of treatment to meet each resident's individual needs. Clinical staff include licensed master's level therapists, certified addiction counselors, peer support specialists, and a licensed practicing psychologist. While living at The Refuge, residents are afforded comprehensive medical and nursing care as well as psychiatric and medication-assisted treatment. As residents progress through the treatment continuum and their needs evolve, they are afforded opportunities for job placement, job skills training and ultimately, transition to sober-living homes, if needed.

items.title: New Castle County Department of Community Services - Housing Authority - Housing Choice Vouchers
items.summary: Housing Choice Vouchers can be used either in public housing units that are operated and maintained by the Public Housing Authority or made available for low-income households to use toward rental assistance in the community. Eligibility includes those with disabilities and elderly persons whose income does not exceed 80% of the local median income. Voucher holders must locate their own unit. The voucher holder pays a portion of the rent each month and the voucher pays the remaining portion. The amount of assistance paid is determined by several factors including income, amount of rent being requested, utilities the renter is responsible for, and the size of the family. Housing Choice Vouchers are transferrable to other units including to another Public Housing Authority jurisdiction. Each Public Housing Authority (PHA) has their own application process and their own way of prioritizing their waitlist. Waitlists are often only open during certain times of the year and applications can only be accepted during those "open" times. It is essential for applicants on a waitlist to keep their contact information and current mailing address updated so they can respond when contacted by a PHA. The New Castle County Dept. of Community Services has a total of 1,825 Vouchers.

data.title: What can I do if my landlord won't return my security deposit?

contentSource.name: Delaware Volunteer Legal Services

data.question: What can I do if my landlord won't return my security deposit?
data.answer: Under Delaware's Landlord-Tenant Code, your landlord has 20 days after you move out to either return your full deposit or send you an itemized list of deductions. If they miss that deadline or the deductions aren't justified, you can send a written demand letter and, if that doesn't work, file a claim in Justice of the Peace Court for double the wrongfully withheld amount.

data.title: How do I apply for SNAP benefits in Delaware?

data.question: How do I apply for SNAP benefits in Delaware?
data.answer: You can apply for SNAP (food stamps) online at Delaware ASSIST (assist.dhss.delaware.gov), by downloading a paper application, or in person at any Division of Social Services State Service Center. You'll need proof of identity, income, and household expenses. Most applications are processed within 30 days, and households in urgent need may qualify for expedited service within 7 days.

data.title: What are my rights if I'm fired without notice in Delaware?
data.summary: Delaware is an at-will employment state, but there are important exceptions worth knowing.

contentSource.name: Community Legal Aid Society

data.question: What are my rights if I'm fired without notice in Delaware?
data.answer: Delaware is an at-will employment state, meaning an employer generally doesn't need a reason or advance notice to end your job. However, you can't be fired for an illegal reason — discrimination based on race, sex, age, disability, or religion; retaliation for filing a workers' comp claim; or retaliation for whistleblowing are all unlawful. If your final paycheck is late, Delaware law requires it within the next regular pay period. If you believe your termination was unlawful, you can file a charge with the Delaware Department of Labor.

data.title: Do I qualify for Medicaid if I'm unemployed?
data.summary: Delaware expanded Medicaid — eligibility is based on household income, not employment status.

contentSource.name: Westside Family Healthcare

data.question: Do I qualify for Medicaid if I'm unemployed?
data.answer: Being unemployed doesn't disqualify you — Delaware expanded Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act, so eligibility is based on household income relative to the Federal Poverty Level, not employment status. A single adult can generally qualify with income up to about 138% of the federal poverty line. You can apply anytime through Delaware ASSIST; there's no separate open-enrollment period for Medicaid.

data.title: How much notice does my landlord have to give before eviction?
data.summary: Notice periods depend on the reason for eviction — from 5 days for nonpayment up to 60 days for no-cause termination of a year-to-year lease.

contentSource.name: Delaware Volunteer Legal Services

data.question: How much notice does my landlord have to give before eviction?
data.answer: It depends on the reason. For nonpayment of rent, a landlord must give 5 days' written notice to pay or quit. For lease violations, it's typically 7 days. To end a month-to-month tenancy without cause, the landlord must give 60 days' notice; for a year-to-year lease, also 60 days before the lease renewal date. In all cases, only a court (Justice of the Peace Court) can actually order you to leave — a landlord cannot lock you out or remove your belongings without a court order.

data.question: Is there help paying my winter heating bill?
data.answer: Yes — the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) provides a one-time grant paid directly to your utility company to help with heating costs. Eligibility is based on household size and income (generally up to 200% of the federal poverty level). Applications open each fall and funds are limited, so it's best to apply as early in the season as possible through your local State Service Center.

data.body:
The Rodney Square Farmers Market returns for its 2026 season beginning Saturday, June 7. The market will run every Saturday from 9am to 1pm through October 31, 2026, in the heart of downtown Wilmington.

This season features more than 20 confirmed local vendors offering fresh produce, dairy, proteins, baked goods, and prepared foods. The market accepts SNAP/EBT benefits, and several vendors participate in the Double Up Food Bucks program, which matches SNAP spending dollar-for-dollar on fresh fruits and vegetables up to $20 per visit.

Rodney Square is located at 1000 N. King Street, Wilmington, DE 19801. Parking is available in nearby garages. The market is accessible via DART bus routes 2, 6, and 11.

contentSource.name: Wilmington Farmers Market

data.why_it_matters: Rodney Square sits in a zip code with limited full-service grocery access. The market's SNAP acceptance and Double Up Food Bucks matching effectively doubles the purchasing power of food assistance benefits for fresh produce.

data.title: Delaware raises income threshold for Emergency Assistance eligibility
data.summary: Effective July 1, Delaware DHSS raised the income threshold for Emergency Assistance — which covers rent, utilities, and emergency shelter — from 100% to 125% of the Federal Poverty Level.
data.body:
The Delaware Department of Health and Social Services (DHSS) announced that the income eligibility threshold for the Emergency Assistance (EA) program will increase from 100% to 125% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL), effective July 1, 2026.

This change expands eligibility for thousands of Delaware households currently just above the cutoff. For a family of four, 125% FPL equals approximately $39,000 per year in 2026.

Emergency Assistance provides one-time funds for rent, utilities, and emergency shelter for households facing an unforeseen crisis. Eligible households must also receive, or be eligible for, Cash Assistance (TANF, GA, or SSI) or certain Medicaid programs.

The change affects applications processed on or after July 1. Households that were denied EA benefits in the past 90 days due to income may reapply after July 1 under the new threshold.

In Wilmington, Emergency Assistance is administered through the Porter State Service Center (509 W. 8th Street) and the Northeast State Service Center (1624 Jessup Street).

contentSource.name: Delaware Health and Social Services

data.why_it_matters: This is a meaningful expansion. Many working families in Wilmington earn just above the old 100% FPL cutoff and have historically been ineligible for Emergency Assistance even during a genuine crisis. The new threshold brings more households into eligibility starting July 1.

data.title: West End Neighborhood House expands Life Lines to age 25
data.summary: West End Neighborhood House has raised the age cap for its Life Lines youth housing program from 23 to 25, effective immediately. The program serves foster care and unaccompanied youth, including LGBTQ+ youth.
data.body:
West End Neighborhood House announced this week that its Life Lines Program — which provides intensive case management, housing support, employment assistance, and life skills instruction to current and former foster care youth — will now serve participants up to age 25, up from the previous cap of 23.

The expansion was driven by data showing that many participants who aged out of the program at 23 were not yet fully housing-stable. The additional two years allows staff to continue working with young adults through a critical period of transition.

The program continues to serve unaccompanied youth and those who identify as LGBTQ+. Services include housing navigation, educational and training program enrollment, financial education, mental health services, medication management, and employment placement assistance.

The Life Lines program is located at 710 N. Lincoln Street, Wilmington, DE 19805. Contact: 302-658-4171.

contentSource.name: West End Neighborhood House

data.why_it_matters: Youth aging out of foster care face some of the highest rates of homelessness of any population. Extending the program by two years directly addresses the gap between structured support and true independence — a period when most young adults still need guidance.

data.body:
Ministry of Caring announced this week that Emmanuel Dining Room — which has served hot meals to Wilmington's hungry for decades — is expanding to seven-day service, adding Sunday hours beginning June 8, 2026.

The dining room is located at 115 East 14th Street, Wilmington, DE 19801. Meals are served at no cost, with no identification or registration required. The expanded Sunday service runs from 11:30am to 1pm.

Ministry of Caring's broader network of services in Wilmington includes multiple emergency shelters, transitional housing programs, dental care, mobile medical services, and early childhood education. The Emmanuel Dining Room expansion was made possible by an increase in volunteer capacity and a grant from a private foundation.

contentSource.name: Ministry of Caring Inc

data.summary: Delaware will begin covering comprehensive dental care for adult Medicaid enrollees on October 1, 2026 — a first for the state. This affects an estimated 70,000 Delaware adults currently on Medicaid.
data.body:
Delaware Governor announced that the state's Medicaid program will begin covering comprehensive dental care for adult enrollees starting October 1, 2026. Previously, adult Medicaid coverage in Delaware was limited to emergency dental extractions only.

The expansion includes preventive care (cleanings, X-rays), restorative services (fillings, crowns), and oral surgery. Orthodontia and cosmetic procedures are not included.

An estimated 70,000 Delaware adults currently enrolled in Medicaid will benefit from the change. No action is required by existing enrollees — coverage activates automatically on October 1.

For Wilmington residents, Ministry of Caring currently operates a dental clinic that serves low-income patients regardless of insurance status. Starting October 1, Ministry of Caring will be able to bill Medicaid directly for covered services, reducing or eliminating out-of-pocket costs for eligible patients.

Residents who are not currently enrolled in Medicaid but believe they may be eligible can apply through Delaware's ASSIST portal at assist.dhss.delaware.gov.

contentSource.name: Delaware Health and Social Services

data.why_it_matters: Dental care has been one of the most significant unmet health needs for low-income Delawareans. Untreated dental problems lead to missed work, school absences, and serious health complications. This expansion removes a major barrier — particularly for residents who've relied on Ministry of Caring's clinic for years.

data.title: Delaware raises income threshold for Emergency Assistance eligibility
data.summary: Effective July 1, Delaware DHSS raised the income threshold for Emergency Assistance — which covers rent, utilities, and emergency shelter — from 100% to 125% of the Federal Poverty Level.
data.body:
The Delaware Department of Health and Social Services (DHSS) announced that the income eligibility threshold for the Emergency Assistance (EA) program will increase from 100% to 125% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL), effective July 1, 2026.

This change expands eligibility for thousands of Delaware households currently just above the cutoff. For a family of four, 125% FPL equals approximately $39,000 per year in 2026.

Emergency Assistance provides one-time funds for rent, utilities, and emergency shelter for households facing an unforeseen crisis. Eligible households must also receive, or be eligible for, Cash Assistance (TANF, GA, or SSI) or certain Medicaid programs.

The change affects applications processed on or after July 1. Households that were denied EA benefits in the past 90 days due to income may reapply after July 1 under the new threshold.

In Wilmington, Emergency Assistance is administered through the Porter State Service Center (509 W. 8th Street) and the Northeast State Service Center (1624 Jessup Street).

contentSource.name: Delaware Health and Social Services

data.why_it_matters: This is a meaningful expansion. Many working families in Wilmington earn just above the old 100% FPL cutoff and have historically been ineligible for Emergency Assistance even during a genuine crisis. The new threshold brings more households into eligibility starting July 1.

data.title: West End Neighborhood House expands Life Lines to age 25
data.summary: West End Neighborhood House has raised the age cap for its Life Lines youth housing program from 23 to 25, effective immediately. The program serves foster care and unaccompanied youth, including LGBTQ+ youth.
data.body:
West End Neighborhood House announced this week that its Life Lines Program — which provides intensive case management, housing support, employment assistance, and life skills instruction to current and former foster care youth — will now serve participants up to age 25, up from the previous cap of 23.

The expansion was driven by data showing that many participants who aged out of the program at 23 were not yet fully housing-stable. The additional two years allows staff to continue working with young adults through a critical period of transition.

The program continues to serve unaccompanied youth and those who identify as LGBTQ+. Services include housing navigation, educational and training program enrollment, financial education, mental health services, medication management, and employment placement assistance.

The Life Lines program is located at 710 N. Lincoln Street, Wilmington, DE 19805. Contact: 302-658-4171.

contentSource.name: West End Neighborhood House

data.why_it_matters: Youth aging out of foster care face some of the highest rates of homelessness of any population. Extending the program by two years directly addresses the gap between structured support and true independence — a period when most young adults still need guidance.

data.title: Aquila Behavioral Health of Delaware
data.summary: The Refuge, a long-term, integrated sober-living facility located in Bear, Delaware. The Refuge provides separate housing units for men and women as well as women with children. These housing environments are supervised around the clock and provide residents support to achieve their sobriety and develop necessary skills to live safely and independently in the community. Structured clinical programs provide varying intensities of treatment to meet each resident's individual needs. Clinical staff include licensed master's level therapists, certified addiction counselors, peer support specialists, and a licensed practicing psychologist. While living at The Refuge, residents are afforded comprehensive medical and nursing care as well as psychiatric and medication-assisted treatment. As residents progress through the treatment continuum and their needs evolve, they are afforded opportunities for job placement, job skills training and ultimately, transition to sober-living homes, if needed.

data.title: New Castle County Department of Community Services - Housing Authority - Housing Choice Vouchers
data.summary: Housing Choice Vouchers can be used either in public housing units that are operated and maintained by the Public Housing Authority or made available for low-income households to use toward rental assistance in the community. Eligibility includes those with disabilities and elderly persons whose income does not exceed 80% of the local median income. Voucher holders must locate their own unit. The voucher holder pays a portion of the rent each month and the voucher pays the remaining portion. The amount of assistance paid is determined by several factors including income, amount of rent being requested, utilities the renter is responsible for, and the size of the family. Housing Choice Vouchers are transferrable to other units including to another Public Housing Authority jurisdiction. Each Public Housing Authority (PHA) has their own application process and their own way of prioritizing their waitlist. Waitlists are often only open during certain times of the year and applications can only be accepted during those "open" times. It is essential for applicants on a waitlist to keep their contact information and current mailing address updated so they can respond when contacted by a PHA. The New Castle County Dept. of Community Services has a total of 1,825 Vouchers.

data.title: YWCA Delaware - Sexual Assault Response Center (SARC)
data.summary: The Sexual Assault Response Center (SARC) provides comprehensive, free and confidential rape crisis services to sexual assault survivors and domestic violence survivors aged 12 and older and their non-offending family members, friends, and partners throughout the State of Delaware. SARC is committed to providing healing, hope and empowerment to individuals whose lives have been impacted by sexual violence whether the assault happened yesterday or many years ago. If you or someone you care about has been sexually assaulted, reaching out for help can be the first step toward recovery and healing. For immediate assistance and information on your options, call our crisis helpline at (800) 773-8570. SARC assists survivors in need of medical, police and legal accompaniment, supportive telephone counseling, aftercare follow-up services, individual and group counseling, as well as information and referral to vital community services. SARC is committed to providing emergency sexual assault and domestic violence responses to all Delawareans who need it. Please note that while the SARC helpline is available 24/7, the wait times for specalized services after regular business hours (6 a.m. to 6 p.m. excluding holidays) may be delayed due to increased requests for our services during these unprecedented times. data.summary: The program seeks to engage families at risk of losing custody of their children in preventative services that helps them overcome the barriers to family safety and stability. This program also serves families who have lost custody of their child but are engaged in the case planning process to be reunified with their child. This program is aimed at providing support and advocacy services to work with each family on an individual level, to address substance abuse issues, mental health concerns, housing issues, employment concerns, domestic violence relationships and positive parenting skills. Families are provided with a Bachelor's or Master's prepared case worker who develops a case plan with the family in conjunction with the Division of Family Services and Delaware Family Courts. The goal of the Family Intervention program is to help primary families achieve safety and stability.

content.title: West End Neighborhood House expands Life Lines to age 25
content.summary: West End Neighborhood House has raised the age cap for its Life Lines youth housing program from 23 to 25, effective immediately. The program serves foster care and unaccompanied youth, including LGBTQ+ youth.

contentSource.name: West End Neighborhood House

content.body:
West End Neighborhood House announced this week that its Life Lines Program — which provides intensive case management, housing support, employment assistance, and life skills instruction to current and former foster care youth — will now serve participants up to age 25, up from the previous cap of 23.

The expansion was driven by data showing that many participants who aged out of the program at 23 were not yet fully housing-stable. The additional two years allows staff to continue working with young adults through a critical period of transition.

The program continues to serve unaccompanied youth and those who identify as LGBTQ+. Services include housing navigation, educational and training program enrollment, financial education, mental health services, medication management, and employment placement assistance.

The Life Lines program is located at 710 N. Lincoln Street, Wilmington, DE 19805. Contact: 302-658-4171.
content.author: manual
content.why_it_matters: Youth aging out of foster care face some of the highest rates of homelessness of any population. Extending the program by two years directly addresses the gap between structured support and true independence — a period when most young adults still need guidance.

content.title: Ministry of Caring's Emmanuel Dining Room expands to seven days a week
content.summary: Emmanuel Dining Room at Ministry of Caring now serves hot meals seven days a week, adding Sunday service for the first time. No ID or registration required.

contentSource.name: Ministry of Caring Inc

content.body:
Ministry of Caring announced this week that Emmanuel Dining Room — which has served hot meals to Wilmington's hungry for decades — is expanding to seven-day service, adding Sunday hours beginning June 8, 2026.

The dining room is located at 115 East 14th Street, Wilmington, DE 19801. Meals are served at no cost, with no identification or registration required. The expanded Sunday service runs from 11:30am to 1pm.

Ministry of Caring's broader network of services in Wilmington includes multiple emergency shelters, transitional housing programs, dental care, mobile medical services, and early childhood education. The Emmanuel Dining Room expansion was made possible by an increase in volunteer capacity and a grant from a private foundation.
content.author: manual
content.why_it_matters: Sunday is historically the hardest day to find a hot meal in Wilmington. Many other food programs are closed on weekends, making this expansion directly address a documented gap in the city's food access network.
